articles.title: CT health providers work to curb HUSKY losses from ‘Big Beautiful’ bill
articles.author: Katy Golvala
articles.body:
Connecticut officials are gearing up for sweeping changes to Medicaid, the joint federal-state program that provides insurance coverage for low-income Americans. Medicaid, known as HUSKY in Connecticut, coversaround939,000 residents, or a quarter of the state’s population.

articles.title: Appeals court upholds ban on immigration enforcement at some churches
articles.author: William J. Ford | Maryland Matters
articles.body:
A federal appeals court Tuesday upheld an injunction that bars Department of Homeland Security agents from conducting immigration enforcement “at or near” more than 1,400 houses of worship sprawling across 33 states and the District of Columbia.

articles.title: The science that protects our children doesn’t take a summer vacation
articles.author: Tony Sheridan
articles.body:
For families, the end of summer can often seem like a never-ending to do list: enjoying the last pool and beach days, shopping for school supplies, and signing up for fall sports and after school activities. articles.title: CT winter heating benefits tick up but still lag pre-pandemic levels
articles.author: Keith M. Phaneuf
articles.body:
Connecticut’s chief heating and energy assistance grant will increase this winter, according to a plan recently approved by state legislators, but aid remains below pre-pandemic levels.

And while the number of fuel distributors participating in the Connecticut Energy Assistance Program also jumped last year, the head of a key trade association said he fears those numbers could shrink dangerously unless reforms are made.

articles.title: Bridgeport exhibit shows Greene Homes through residents’ eyes: ‘It’s our story to tell’
articles.author: Reginald David
articles.body:
Inside the Charles F. Greene Homes public housing complex, residents have learned to live with elevators that break down often, mold in aging buildings, broken windows, unsafe basements and hallways where strangers sometimes gather.

articles.title: UConn Hartford opens its first set of dorms in the city
articles.author: Abigail Brone | Connecticut Public
articles.body:
Pratt Street in downtown Hartford was quiet Monday morning as University of Connecticut alumni and officials gathered to cut the ribbon on UConn Hartford’s first dormitory.

Kai Blatchford, a UConn junior majoring in social work, previously attended UConn’s main campus in Storrs, but Blatchford decided to enroll at UConn Hartford and live at the new dorm to be more integrated with the communities he wanted to help through his major.

articles.title: Will CT’s new healthcare affordability measures lower costs?
articles.author: Katy Golvala
articles.body:

articles.title: SHU Poll: Housing Cost Concerns Unite Voters, MAGA Label More Unpopular Than Democratic Socialist
articles.author: Donald Eng
articles.body: Seven in 10 Democrats (70.1%) and nearly as many Republicans (68.8%) say housing affordability will be one of the most important issues in deciding their vote for governor. Independents also place significant importance on the issue, with 63.7% ranking housing costs among their top concerns.

articles.title: DECD Improves Handling Of CT’s Media Tax Credits, Audit Finds
articles.author: Viktoria Sundqvist
articles.body: Production companies with at least $100,000 in Connecticut expenditures that conduct at least 50% of their principal photography in Connecticut, expend at least 50% of postproduction costs in the state, or incur at least $1 million in in-state postproduction costs are eligible for tax credits.

articles.title: CT Seeks Public Feedback On State Rail Plan
articles.author: Staff Report
articles.body: The rail plan is a federally required planning document that establishes a vision for passenger and freight rail transportation throughout the state and identifies strategies, policies, and potential investments to support Connecticut's rail network. The plan helps guide future rail priorities and investments, supports economic activity and mobility, and informs transportation-related decisions across Connecticut and the broader Northeast region, according to DOT officials.

articles.title: Kennedy’s Quiet Hunt For Autism Culprits Stalls As Trump Orders Baseless Changes To Childhood Shots
articles.author: Amanda Seitz and Stephanie Armour, KFF Health News
articles.body: President Donald Trump has ordered a reduction in childhood vaccines — publicly faulting the shots for an increase in autism cases — even as the nation’s top health official, Robert F. Kennedy Jr., has failed to produce evidence linking vaccinations to the disorder.
